record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space of dimension at least 3, and write S_X for its unit sphere. Is X necessarily a Hilbert space if every closed homogeneous hyperplane H in X admits a unit vector x in S_X such that x is isosceles-orthogonal to all unit vectors of H, meaning x ⊥_I y for every y in H ∩ S_X, where isosceles orthogonality is the relation ∥x - y∥ = ∥x + y∥?

evidence.quote: Question 4.6.22 Let X be a Banach space, dim X ≥ 3, such that for any closed and homogeneous hyperplane H ⊂ X there exists x ∈ SX such that x ⊥I Hx ∩ SX . Is X necessarily a Hilbert space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space with $\dim X \geq 3$, and let $S_X = \{x \in X : \|x\| = 1\}$ denote its unit sphere. For $x, y \in X$, say that $x$ is isosceles-orthogonal to $y$, written $x \perp_I y$, if $\|x - y\| = \|x + y\|$. A closed homogeneous hyperplane in $X$ is a closed linear subspace $H \subset X$ of codimension $1$.

Suppose $X$ has the following property: for every closed homogeneous hyperplane $H \subset X$, there exists a unit vector $x \in S_X$ such that 
$$x \perp_I y \quad \text{for every } y \in H \cap S_X.$$
Must $X$ be a Hilbert space?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the existence, for each closed homogeneous hyperplane, of a unit vector isosceles-orthogonal to that hyperplane forces a Banach space of dimension at least 3 to be a Hilbert space is posed as an open problem in the literature on orthogonality types. General web search returns related work on isosceles-orthogonality constants and Hilbert space characterizations, but no resolution of this specific hyperplane condition was found.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric form geometric constant related to isosceles orthogonality in Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Isosceles orthogonality (||x+y||=||x-y||) was introduced by James in 1945; numerous characterizations of Hilbert spaces via orthogonality conditions exist, but the hyperplane-version remains discussed as a question.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study isosceles orthogonality and Hilbert-space characterizations without resolving the hyperplane condition.

status_evidence.title: On some results on linear orthogonality spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys orthogonality types in normed linear spaces including isosceles orthogonality and lists characterization problems for Hilbert spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Survey literature treats the hyperplane existence property as one of several open characterization problems.
